3.title: Introduce yourself in German (for absolute beginners)
3.focus: Real people answer five basic questions. Listen for the question, then the answer, and repeat the answers aloud. Then answer the same five questions about yourself.

questions.q: Several people answer “Ich komme aus Berlin” or “Ich komme aus Zürich”. Which question are they answering?
questions.why: woher = where from.

questions.q: Wo lebst du? – Ich ___ in Berlin. (wohnen)
questions.why: Both wohne and lebe appear in the video.

questions.q: A man answers “Ich bin Student.” Which question is this the answer to?
questions.why: Beruf = profession; Ich bin Student/Lehrer answers it.

4.title: GERMAN LESSON 19: EASY Conjugation of German REGULAR VERBS (+ Personal Pronouns)
4.focus: Follow the verb kommen through all pronouns: ich komme, du kommst, er/sie/es kommt … Then do Anja’s homework and conjugate wohnen yourself.

questions.q: Anja’s table: ich komme, du ___, er kommt.
questions.why: Regular verbs: du takes -st.

questions.q: According to Anja, how does the infinitive of about 99 % of German verbs end?
questions.why: kommen, wohnen, machen … remove -en and add the personal ending.

questions.q: Which verb does Anja give as homework to conjugate?
questions.why: ich wohne, du wohnst, er wohnt …

5.title: Counting in German from 1 – 100 (German Numbers for Beginners)
5.focus: Count along out loud. Notice the pattern for 13–19, the -zig endings for tens, and the surprising order in numbers like 37.

questions.q: Which numbers between 10 and 20 have no clear pattern, according to the video?
questions.why: elf and zwölf are special; 13–19 are built as number + zehn.

questions.q: How do Germans say 37?
questions.why: The unit comes first: sieben und dreißig.

questions.q: 13 = drei + zehn = ___ (one word)
questions.why: drei + zehn.

6.title: GERMAN LESSON 23: The 6 Most IMPORTANT German Question Words!
6.focus: Learn the six W-words with their example questions. Write one question of your own for each word.

questions.q: Which question word asks about time? (Wann kommst du nach Hause?)
questions.why: wann = when.

questions.q: ___ ist die Toilette? (Where is the toilet?)
questions.why: wo = where.

questions.q: Which question word means “why”?
questions.why: Anja’s example: Warum ist die Banane krumm?

7.title: GERMAN LESSON 9: The German Definite Articles DER, DIE, DAS
7.focus: Listen for the two big tips: always learn a noun with its article, and the -chen ending. Write down the six example nouns Anja gives.

questions.q: What is Anja’s most important tip for learning German nouns?
o: Learn every noun together with its article
questions.why: Always der Apfel, not just Apfel.

questions.q: Why is it “das Mädchen” although a girl is female?
o: Words ending in -chen are always neuter
Girls are grammatically neuter in every language
It is a mistake in the dictionary
questions.why: -chen makes a diminutive: das Mädchen, das Brötchen.

questions.q: Which article goes with “Frau” in Anja’s examples?
questions.why: die Frau, der Mann, das Kind.

8.title: How to Order in a German Restaurant
8.focus: Pick up the phrases in order: arriving, asking for the menu, ordering, asking for a recommendation. Practise the short waiter–guest dialogue aloud.

questions.q: How do you ask for a table for two people?
o: Haben Sie einen Tisch für zwei Personen?
Wo ist die Speisekarte für zwei?
questions.why: Tisch = table, Personen = people.

questions.q: Können wir ___ sitzen? (outside)
questions.why: draußen = outside, drinnen = inside.

questions.q: How do you politely order a red wine?
questions.why: Ich hätte gerne … = I would like …

9.title: “haben” and “sein” in the Past Tense (Präteritum Guide)
9.source: YouTube · Learn German with Herr Antrim
9.focus: Follow the conjugation tables for hatte and war, then read every example sentence aloud. Note which past tense he says Germans prefer for these two verbs.

questions.q: Which past tense do most Germans use in speech for haben and sein?
questions.why: For haben and sein the short Präteritum forms are the natural choice in speech.

questions.q: Ich ___ gestern im Kino. (sein, past)
questions.why: ich war, du warst, er war …

questions.q: “As a child I ___ a lot of toys.” Which German form fits?
questions.why: ich hatte.

10.title: Learn German Vocabulary – Countries & Languages in German (Länder und Sprachen)
10.focus: Repeat each pair aloud (country, then language). Notice that most language names end in -isch. Make a note of the countries that come with an article.

questions.q: Which language do people speak in Österreich?
questions.why: Österreich – Deutsch, as in the video.

questions.q: Spanien – ___ (the language)
questions.why: Spanien – Spanisch.

questions.q: Which of these country names comes with an article?
questions.why: die Türkei, die USA, die Schweiz.

11.title: GERMAN LESSON 15: The German indefinite articles EIN and EINE
11.focus: Sort each of Anja’s example nouns by gender. Do her mini exercise at the end (Stift, Flasche, Kissen, Kartoffeln) before she gives the solution.

questions.q: How many indefinite articles does German have (in the nominative)?
questions.why: ein for masculine and neuter, eine for feminine.

questions.q: die Schüssel → das ist ___ Schüssel
questions.why: Feminine nouns take eine.

questions.q: Which indefinite article is used with plural nouns such as “Schuhe”?
questions.why: das sind Schuhe – no article in the plural.

12.title: How to Negate German Sentences – NICHT vs. KEIN for Beginners
12.focus: Watch how nicht changes position, then how kein replaces ein/eine. Make your own negated version of each example.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
questions.why: With a plain verb, nicht comes after it.

questions.q: “Das Auto ist neu.” – negated:
questions.why: With an adjective, nicht stands before it.

questions.q: Ich habe eine Tochter. → Ich habe ___ Tochter.
questions.why: Negating ein/eine + noun: kein / keine.

13.title: My new house! Learn German Vocabulary of Furniture and Rooms!
13.focus: Walk through Anja’s house room by room and write down each room and piece of furniture with its article. Her homework: write a few sentences about your own home.

questions.q: Anja explains “das Wohnzimmer”. Which two parts is it built from?
questions.why: The living room is the room to live in.

questions.q: What does “der Kühlschrank” mean literally?
questions.why: kühl = cool, der Schrank = cupboard: fridge.

questions.q: What is the plural of “das Fahrrad”, as Anja says?
questions.why: das Fahrrad – die Fahrräder.

14.title: LESSON 16: Learn the German POSSESSIVE PRONOUNS: Mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser …
14.focus: Write the list mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer, ihr/Ihr next to the pronouns ich, du, er, sie … and watch which endings appear with feminine and plural nouns.

questions.q: ich → mein, du → ___, er → sein
questions.why: dein = your (informal).

questions.q: “Das ist sein Ball.” means:
questions.why: sein = his (and also “to be”, as Anja jokes).

questions.q: Which possessive means “her” (for a woman)?
questions.why: ihr Ball = her ball.

15.title: GERMAN LESSON 46: German Separable Verbs Explained – Trennbare Verben
15.focus: Notice how the prefix jumps to the end of the sentence. Say each of Anja’s examples aloud, then make two of your own with aufstehen and einkaufen.

questions.q: “Der Zug fährt um 9 Uhr ab.” Where does the prefix “ab” stand?
o: At the end of the sentence
questions.why: The prefix of a separable verb goes to the end in main clauses.

questions.q: What is the infinitive in “Der Zug fährt ab”?
questions.why: ab + fahren = to depart.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
o: Ich stehe auf um 7 Uhr früh dann.
questions.why: aufstehen → ich stehe … auf.

16.title: Learn German Vocabulary – Hobbies in German (Hobbys)
16.focus: Repeat every hobby aloud and then say the two model sentences with your own hobbies.

questions.q: How do you say “My hobby is cooking”?
questions.why: Mein Hobby ist + infinitive.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct for two hobbies?
o: Meine Hobbys sind lesen und Musik hören.
Mein Hobbys ist lesen und Musik hören.
questions.why: Plural: meine Hobbys sind …

questions.q: How does the video say “Ski” in “Skifahren” should be pronounced at the start?
questions.why: Ski is pronounced “schi”.

17.title: GERMAN LESSON 59: How to tell the TIME in German – Die Uhrzeit (part 1)
17.focus: Say every clock time out loud with Anja. Watch how she adds 12 to get the 24-hour time and how halb works.

questions.q: How do you ask what time it is?
questions.why: Also: Wie viel Uhr ist es?

questions.q: How does Anja say 4 pm in the 24-hour style?

questions.why: halb fünf – half of the way to five.

18.title: Learn German | German Grammar | Modalverben | Modal verbs | A1
18.focus: List the six modal verbs and note the structure: conjugated modal verb in position 2, infinitive at the very end.

questions.q: How many modal verbs are there in German?
questions.why: dürfen, können, mögen, müssen, sollen, wollen.

questions.q: In a sentence with a modal verb, where does the second verb (infinitive) go?
questions.why: Ich kann gut schwimmen.

questions.q: Ich ___ gut schwimmen. (können)
questions.why: ich kann, du kannst, er kann.
